newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers call for wider curbs on water usage.
newsitem.headline: French farmers call for wider curbs on water usage.

text.p: France's largest farm union said on Friday that cities and industries and not just farmers must be made to limit the amount of water they can use in the face of mounting drought fears.
"Farming, industry and the cities must participate on a fair basis in water control," said Jean Dube, the head of the FNSEA's drought crisis team.
Dube was speaking after the special team held its first meeting on Friday.
The group was set up to keep track of crop conditions across the nation after a three-month dry spell raised fears of crop losses and pushed up grain prices.
Persistent dry weather has forced local athorities in 13 departments including the Beauce grain belt to limit the amount of water farmers can use to irrigate crops.
But farmers now say these limits must be extended to other sectors of the economy.
The FNSEA proposes for instance that cities limit the sprinkling of lawns and car wash operations, Dube said.
Farmers are often singled out as major water users but cities consume 2.5 billion cubic metres of water each year, roughly the same amount as farmers, he said.

Rainfall has been as much as 50 percent below normal since January in the north of France and even lower in the south. But some relief may be in sight as French meteorological services have forecast rain for the weekend.
The farm ministry said this week it was setting up an aid programme to compensate farmers for damage caused by drought.
